main_text.head: CONCIO XXVI.
Proverb. 14.

p.i: Mulieres sapientes instaurant domum suam, stulta autem manibus suis evertet eam.
Qui ambulat in rectitudine sua, timet Dominum: qui autem se avertit a viis eius, despicit eum.
In ore stulti est virga superbia : labia autem sapientum conservant eos.
Ubi boves non sunt, ibi praesepe vacuum est: & ubi multa sunt fruges (hapro veniunt) viribus bovis [?].

main_text.p: 1 Quomodo pia & felix instituenda sit οἰκονομία[?], docet hîc Salomon. Est autem eligenda vxor non infipiens, etiamsi diues aut nobilis, aut pulchra sit, sed sapiens, iuxta illud Siracidæ cap. 7. μὴ ἀσχ[illegible, ~40 letters]. Nam, uti-dem inquit, cap. 36. qui bonam vxorem nactus est, principium habet facultatum, adiutorem sibi accommodatum, & columnam in qua conquiescat. Hoc non perpendunt, qui vel pecuniæ cupiditate, vel ambitione capti præcipitantur in nuptias: nescientes nobilitatis & amplæ dotis duo pessima mala socia esse, vxoris superbiam, & viri seruitutem. Itaque non iniuria apud Plautum veretur ille magnatem, dotatamque matronam duce-

page.notes: Running head "NUPTIALES." and page number "173" are read from a small scan; the digits are uncertain. The initial M is a woodcut, joined to "ulieres" as "Mulieres". Long s is plain s throughout. Printed "vbi"/"Vbi" was changed to "ubi"/"Ubi" and "boues" to "boves", "conferuant" to "conservant" under the u/v rule. Final word "bouis" is printed as shown and read as "bovis" with [?]; it may be a misprint for "bonis". The Greek word after "instituenda sit" is read as οἰκονομία but is doubtful. The Greek Sirach quotation (cap. 7) is too faint to read and is marked illegible. The number after "cap." in "cap. 36." is doubtful. The parenthetical "(hapro veniunt)" is printed in Latin letters as shown. The paragraph ends mid-word with "duce-" as printed, and continues on the next page. A stray comma-like mark at the right edge is not text and is omitted.
